England primary maths · Year 2

Year 2 maths.
Stronger basics, one match at a time.

Place value and calculations to 100. The 2, 5 and 10 tables with division. Thirds, quarters, five-minute time, money and data. Use the academy alongside teaching and practical learning.

Build a Year 2 player

What does Year 2 practice focus on?

01

Place value and calculations to 100

02

The 2, 5 and 10 tables with division

03

Thirds, quarters, five-minute time, money and data

The map below names 40 practice families available for this year. Supporting skills can be revisited when a pupil needs them. Schools may sequence content differently within a key stage.

The Year 2 skills map

Number

Count in steps

Count in 2s, 3s and 5s; add or subtract 10.

Tens and ones

Represent two-digit numbers using place value.

Numbers and words to 100

Read and write numbers to at least 100.

Order and compare to 100

Use <, > and = and choose greatest or smallest.

Number lines to 100

Locate values using equal intervals.

Odd and even

Connect parity with pairs and the 2 table.

Add & subtract

Addition within 10

Little numbers. A strong start.

Subtraction within 10

Take away and find what is left.

Make 10

Find the two parts that make 10.

Addition across 10

Make 10, then add the rest.

Subtraction across 10

Step back to 10, then keep going.

Make 20

Build on the bonds you already know.

Doubles & halves

Two equal parts, both ways round.

Missing numbers

Use what you know to find the gap.

Two-digit addition and subtraction

Calculate with ones, tens and two-digit values.

Add three numbers

Add three one-digit numbers efficiently.

Related facts to 100

Derive larger facts from number bonds.

Inverse and order

Check calculations; distinguish commutativity and inverse.

Two-step number stories

Work through addition and subtraction contexts.

Times & divide

The 2 times table

Build every fact from 2 × 1 to 2 × 12.

The 5 times table

Build every fact from 5 × 1 to 5 × 12.

The 10 times table

Build every fact from 10 × 1 to 10 × 12.

Mix the 2, 5 and 10s

Mix the 2, 5 and 10s

Division: 2, 5 and 10

Division: 2, 5 and 10

Arrays and equal groups

Connect multiplication and division with pictures and stories.

Fractions & decimals

Thirds and quarters

Find 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of shapes and amounts.

Two quarters make a half

Connect simple equivalent fractions.

Measure & time

Units and tools

Choose m/cm, kg/g, litres/ml and degrees Celsius.

Pounds, pence and change

Find totals, differences and change.

Make the same amount

Combine coins in different ways.

Time to five minutes

Read five-minute intervals and quarter past/to.

Set five-minute times

Construct an analogue time.

Hours and minutes

Compare intervals; use 60 minutes and 24 hours.

Shapes & space

2D properties

Count sides; recognise symmetry.

Faces, edges and vertices

Describe flat faces and solid properties.

Lines of symmetry

Recognise and complete a symmetric figure.

Shape and number patterns

Predict a repeating pattern.

Directions and right-angle turns

Use clockwise, anticlockwise and right-angle turns.

Charts & tables

Tallies, tables and pictures

Read categories, totals and differences.

Build a block diagram

Represent given category counts.

Recall and connections

Times tables in Year 2

Build the 2, 5 and 10 tables and their related division facts. Counting in 3s is included, while the 3 table recall focus comes in Year 3.

Times-table guide

Beyond a number answer

A grown-up records practical and reasoning work alongside digital practice.

  • Choose and use measuring tools
  • Make thirds and quarters
  • Draw and explain a time
  • Sort shapes and demonstrate turns
  • Make a tally and pictogram
  • Explain a calculation

How Year 2 promotion works

XP rewards effort and independent answers, but does not award a completed year. The academy checks broad independent coverage and later-day recall across this year’s families. Practical observations are recorded by a grown-up. A 12-shot promotion match then requires at least 90% independent accuracy, with the other goals still satisfied. Earlier facts remain available for review after promotion.

This is an in-game progression policy. It is not a DfE-approved pass mark, a diagnostic judgement or a guarantee that a skill will never be forgotten.
